title: The AI Arsenal That Could Stop World War III | Palmer Luckey | TED
summary: A defence-tech founder argues the US would lose a Taiwan war for lack of mass, and that cheap, mass-produced autonomous AI weapons would restore deterrence against China.

assertions.quote: By deploying autonomous systems at scale, this type of autonomous system, we prove to our adversaries that we have the capacity to win.

verdicts.note: Untested; deterrence depends on many factors and autonomous mass has not been fielded at scale in the Pacific.

assertions.quote: The United States exhausts its shallow arsenal of precision munitions in a mere eight days.
we don't have enough. Not enough weapons, not enough platforms to carry those weapons.
China has the world's largest navy, with 232 times the shipbuilding capacity of the United States
producing over 90 percent of most advanced semiconductors

verdicts.note: TSMC produces roughly nine in ten of the world's leading-edge logic chips.

assertions.quote: If those factories are seized or destroyed, the global economy will crash overnight.
Our destroyers’ Aegis systems are capable of locking on and firing on targets totally autonomously.

verdicts.note: Loitering munitions and air defences have autonomous modes, but documented use with no human target approval is rare and disputed.

assertions.quote: Countries only go to war when they disagree as to who the victor will be.

verdicts.note: Disagreement about relative power is one recognised cause of war, but commitment problems and indivisible stakes also cause wars, so 'only' is too strong.

assertions.quote: It increases precision. It reduces collateral damage.

verdicts.note: Precision weapons have cut collateral damage compared with area bombing, but AI targeting has not been shown to reduce civilian harm and may speed up strikes.
